title: Aubergine Rollatini
subtitle: Oven-baked aubergine rolls filled with ricotta and spinach
excerpt: Thin slices of aubergine roasted until pliable, then rolled around a seasoned ricotta and spinach filling and baked in tomato passata. A proper Italian-American Sunday dish that holds well and reheats beautifully.
sourceNotes: Italian-American tradition, common across New York and New Jersey Italian restaurants and home kitchens.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking or after. Cover tightly. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 30 minutes covered, then 10 minutes uncovered.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and fill two dishes. Both bake at the same time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the rolls and refrigerate up to 24 hours before baking.

content.text: Rollatini works when the aubergine slices are thin enough to roll without cracking. Roast them first to drive off moisture and make them pliable. Keep the ricotta filling fairly dry or the rolls will weep into the sauce.

Heat the oven to 190C. Brush the aubergine slices on both sides with olive oil. Lay them on baking trays in a single layer. Roast for 18 minutes, turning once, until soft and lightly golden. Leave to cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, grated mozzarella, half the parmesan, the beaten egg, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Stir in the spinach until evenly combined.
Spread the passata across the base of the gratin dish in an even layer.
Lay each aubergine slice flat. Spoon a heaped tablespoon of the ricotta mixture along the shorter end. Roll the slice up firmly and place it seam-side down in the sauce. Repeat with all slices.
Scatter the torn mozzarella and remaining parmesan over the top. Drizzle with a little olive oil.
Bake for 25 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the edges of the rolls are beginning to colour. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The rolls break apart when I lift them.
items.cause: The aubergine was too thick or under-roasted and split when rolled.
items.fix: Slice no thicker than 5mm and roast until fully pliable before filling.

items.cause: The spinach was not squeezed dry enough.
items.fix: Wring the spinach in a clean cloth until almost no liquid comes out.

items.symptom: The rolls float in sauce instead of holding shape.
items.cause: Too much passata, or the dish is too large.
items.fix: Use just enough passata to cover the base in a thin layer, and choose a dish that holds the rolls snugly.
